questions.question: Describe the purpose of hacking from a security perspective.
questions.solution_html:
• Purpose of hacking is to identify and exploit vulnerabilities in a computer systems and
  • networks to gain unauthorized access or control

questions.solution_html:
• Identify the cyber crime that involves creating fake websites to deceive users. / [CO1]
  • Phishing – Identification- (1 mark)

questions.question: Describe exploitation phase in Ethical Hacking.
questions.solution_html:
• The exploitation phase involves leveraging vulnerabilities identified during previous stages
  • to gain unauthorized access to a target system or network.

questions.question: Describe Reconnaissance.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe Reconnaissance. / [CO1]
  • Reconnaissance is the information-gathering stage of ethical hacking, where you collect
  • data about the target system before launching an attack.
  • Explanation – (1 mark)

questions.question: Explain the role of the Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act (CISA).
questions.solution_html:
• CISA is a U.S. federal law that promotes collaboration between private sector and
  • government agencies to enhance cybersecurity by facilitating the sharing of threat
  • information and defensive measures.

questions.question: Explain the punishment for hacking under the IT Act.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the punishment for hacking under the IT Act. / [CO1]
  • Section 66 - Imprisonment up to 3 years Or fine up to ₹5 lakh Or both.
  • Explanation – (1 mark)

questions.question: Identify the cyber crime that involves sending fraudulent emails to steal personal information.
questions.solution_html: • phishing attack

questions.question: Name the three types of hacking and state one key feature for each.
questions.solution_html:
• Name the three types of hacking and state one key feature for each. / [CO1]
  • * White Hat Hacking (Ethical Hacking) - Key Feature: Performed legally to identify and fix
  • security vulnerabilities.
  • * Black Hat Hacking - Key Feature: Performed illegally with malicious intent such as
  • stealing data or causing damage.
  • * Grey Hat Hacking - Key Feature: Accesses systems without permission but usually not
  • for personal gain; may disclose vulnerabilities later.
  • Listing 3 types – ½ mark. Stating key feature – ½ mark

questions.question: Explain the types of phishing is in cyber crime.
questions.solution_html: • email phishing ,spear phishing, smishing(SMS),vishing(voice),whaling ,angler phishing

questions.question: Describe clearing tracks in ethical hacking.
questions.solution_html:
• clearing tracks: Remove any evidence of the ethical hacking activity to mimic real -world
  • attackers and ensure systems are left as they were.

questions.question: Explain the term ‘digital signature’ refer to in cyber law.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the term ‘digital signature’ refer to in cyber law. / [CO1]
  • A digital signature is an electronic method used to verify the authenticity, integrity, and
  • identity - (1 mark)

questions.question: Describe white hat hacking.
questions.solution_html:
• Also known as ethical hacking refers to the practice of using hacking techniques for
  • legitimate purpose such as identifying and fixing security vulnerabilities in a computer
  • systems ,networks, or software.

questions.question: Why do attackers clear logs after post-exploitation?
questions.solution_html:
• Why do attackers clear logs after post-exploitation? / [CO1]
  • Attackers clear logs after post-exploitation to hide their activities and avoid detection or
  • forensic investigation. – (1 mark)

questions.question: Identify the section of the IT Act that deals with identity theft.
questions.solution_html: • Formal definition, mathematical statement, and illustrative example answering Identify the section of the IT Act that deals with identity theft. . (2 Marks)

questions.question: Describe exploitation.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe exploitation. / [CO1]
  • Exploitation is the process of taking advantage of a vulnerability in a computer system,
  • network, or application to gain unauthorized access or perform malicious actions. – (1 mark)

questions.question: Define threat .
questions.solution_html:
• Threat refers to any potential danger(anything that could exploit a vulnerability) that could
  • harm systems ,data, or operations.

questions.question: Define Packet inspection firewall.
questions.solution_html:
• Define Packet inspection firewall. / [CO2]
  • A packet inspection firewall is a firewall that examines data packets passing through a
  • network and allows or blocks them based on security rules. – (1 mark)

questions.question: Define Dictionary Attacks.
questions.solution_html:
• Dictionary Attacks: Where the hackers attempt to crack passwords by trying various words
  • and phrases from a predefined list or dictionary ,against a password -protected systems.

questions.question: Define Vulnerability .
questions.solution_html:
• Define Vulnerability. / [CO2]
  • A vulnerability is a weakness or flaw in a computer system, network, or software that
  • can be exploited by an attacker to cause harm or gain unauthorized access. – (1 mark)

questions.question: Many cyberattacks begin with an initial-------------------- phase. [1x10 = 10]
questions.solution_html: • Reconnaissance Phase

questions.question: Describe malware attack. [1x10 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe malware attack. / [CO2]
  • A malware attack is a cyber attack in which malicious software is used to damage,
  • disrupt, steal data from, or gain unauthorized access to a computer system or network. – (1 mark)
  • [1x10 = 10]

questions.question: Compare the ethical and legal implications of white hat hacking versus black hat hacking.
questions.solution_html:
• white hat hackers ,authorized by the target organization ,use their skills to find and report
  • vulnerabilities for the purpose of improving system security.This is ethical because they
  • operate with consent and legal authorization ,aiming to enhance security. Black hat hacking
  • ,on the other hand ,is illegal and unethical.

questions.question: What are the main components of reporting?
questions.solution_html:
• What are the main components of reporting? / [CO1]
  • Executive Summary, Technical Report, Findings and Vulnerabilities, Risk Assessment,
  • Recommendations/Remediation, Supporting Evidence and Conclusion.
  • Listing out components – (2 marks)
  • Detailed explanation – (3 marks)

questions.question: What is post-exploitation in ethical hacking, and why is it important?
questions.solution_html:
• Post exploitation :Gather intelligence and asses the potential impact of the compromise.
  • (Data Exfiltration ,System Monitoring, Lateral Movement)

questions.question: Discuss how Ethical Hackers can get Hands-On Practice Gaining Access.
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss how Ethical Hackers can get Hands-On Practice Gaining Access. / [CO1]
  • Ethical hackers can get hands-on practice gaining access by using legal and controlled
  • environments to learn hacking techniques and security testing methods. - Virtual Labs, Practice
  • Platforms, Capture The Flag (CTF) Challenges, Penetration Testing Tools,
  • Detailed explanation – (5 marks)

questions.question: Differentiate between Ransomware and Spyware.
questions.solution_html:
• Ransomware encrypts or locks a victim’s data or system ,demanding a ransom payment
  • for its release. Spyware, on the other hand ,gathers and transmits information from a user’s
  • device without their knowledge ,such as passwords ,browsing history and financial details.

questions.question: Discuss how to prevent cyber attack.
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss how to prevent cyber attack. / [CO2]
  • Cyber attacks can be prevented by adopting proper security measures and safe online
  • practices - Use Strong Passwords, Install Antivirus and Firewall, Regular Software Updates, Use
  • Secure Networks, Access Control and Authentication, Security Awareness Training, Regular
  • Security Audits etc.
  • Detailed explanation – (5 marks)

questions.question: How Phishing Works? [5x3 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• Phishing works by luring victims with fraudulent emails messages or calls that mimic
  • legitimate communications from trusted sources .These messages often include malicious
  • links or attachments designed to steal sensitive information like credentials ,credit details ,or
  • personal data.

questions.question: Differentiate Phishing and Spoofing. [5x3 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate Phishing and Spoofing. / [CO2]
  • Phishing is a cyber attack used to steal sensitive information from users. Spoofing is a
  • technique used to disguise/fake the sender's identity. Spoofing hides the attacker's identity, and
  • phishing tries to trick users into giving important information.
  • Phishing and spoofing definition – (2 marks)
  • Explain differences – (3 marks)
  • [5x3 = 15]

questions.question: Explain the difference between Packet filter firewalls, Packet inspection firewalls. [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Packet filter firewall-Analyze network traffic based on simple rules like IP
  • addresses,port,and protocols .
  • Packet inspection firewall-(specifically ,stateful inspection )maintain a “state table” to track
  • connections and make decisions based on the packets history and connection state .
